Multiplayer and feature limits

Play together on your local network, then check the limits that still apply.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Multiplayer

Good to know. Use the same game build on both computers and a trusted local network. Multiplayer still has limits; it is not complete parity with solo play. Join a multiplayer world Multiplayer menu: Host this world (LAN hosting)

Host your world

  1. Open Multiplayer on the main menu and choose Host this world.
  2. Read the join address shown. Other players can choose your world from their LAN list, or type that complete address and port into SERVER. Multiplayer menu: list of worlds hosted on the LAN
  3. Keep the host computer on and connected. Opening Main menu keeps hosting.
  4. Choose Stop hosting to disconnect other players and return to solo play with the recovered world and pack. If the world cannot be saved when you stop, you stay hosted; fix the reported problem, such as a full disk, and choose Stop hosting again. If you are sitting or lying on furniture and the space beside it is blocked, saving and stopping wait until you can stand up safely. Clear the space or get up, then try again.

If hosting has stopped but pack recovery fails, keep the game open. Continue returns to the repair session, F6 retries, and Shift+F6 opens a recovery choice. Follow Saves and world files before discarding any state.

Join a world

  1. Open Multiplayer. Choose a LAN world or one of your last eight servers, or type HOST or HOST:PORT in SERVER. The default port is 27015.
  2. Enter your display name in NAME; leave it empty to use your login name, or Player if none is set. Tab switches fields.
  3. Choose Join server or press Enter. Esc cancels while joining. Your local world is saved before joining; the server world is kept by its host.

Each player has a separate inventory. Crafting, storage, Survival needs and recovery wait for the server, and the status line says when an action is waiting. Only the world's saved owner has a Home crate; see Your first survival day. Boats and some other actions remain limited. A refusal message explains when an action is unavailable.

Press Enter to type a chat message, Enter again to send it, or Esc to cancel. Multiplayer chat

Careful. The first server certificate is remembered. If it changes, joining is refused; check the server identity before changing saved trust.

For the separate server program and console commands, see Run a dedicated server (voxelgame-server).

Saving on a server

  • In a world you joined, F6 writes nothing on your computer and says 'This session does not save the world locally'. The server keeps that world. While you host, F6 saves your hosted world as usual.
  • A dedicated server confirms an action that changes your items, needs or the world, such as crafting, eating, building, storing or respawning, only after it has saved the change. Refusals arrive at once.
  • If the dedicated server cannot save, the action keeps waiting until a later save works, and it is never carried out twice. If you disconnect while waiting, rejoin and check your pack and the world before trying again.
  • Near the 8 MiB save limit, any server refuses an action that would make its world file too big, for example 'Crafting would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid'. Refused crafting keeps its ingredients.

Creative on a server

  • When you join a Creative server, Home, chest and furniture storage move only the supplies you really carry on the server, listed as Carried supplies. Free catalogue items stay separate and cannot be stored.
  • As the Creative host, wait for your pack to be confirmed before using storage. The Home tab says 'Home storage waits for pack confirmation' until then.
  • The world's saved owner can build, repair, rest at and pack up the Home crate in Creative too. The crate is free, and packing it up gives no boards.
  • You can move and turn furniture that was paid for in Survival. It is not charged again and still refunds its materials when it is later taken up in Survival. Moving filled kitchen storage keeps what is inside.

Fire

Planned, not in the game. There is no fire you can light, spread or put out. Explosions show a brief flash and burst and leave nothing burning. Fire

The FIRE & FOOD crafting tab holds recipes only: charcoal, cooked meat, glass and flasks are crafted there from the pack, with no campfire or furnace to place. Charcoal, cooking and glass (no furnace)

Planned, not in the game. Campfires, furnaces and spreading fire are not in the game yet.

Lava

Planned, not in the game. There is no lava liquid. Volcanic areas and lava tubes are solid rock: basalt, obsidian, lava rock, pahoehoe and magma stone. Lava tubes are cooled and walkable. Nothing flows, burns or cools into stone. Lava
Good to know. Only water flows in this version, so there is no lava pool to avoid.

Waterfalls

Planned, not in the game. There are no natural waterfalls. Water you place in creative mode can pour over an edge, but no cascade is drawn and the waterfall sound is not used. Natural waterfalls and dripstone caves

Caves cut through limestone do have stalagmites, stalactites and joined columns in worlds made with the current generator. See Caves and geological landmarks.

Furniture limits

The furniture plans cover chairs, stools, benches, armchairs, sofas, single and double beds, wardrobes, chests of drawers, a bookcase, a wall shelf, dining tables, writing desks, coffee and side tables, floor and table lamps, a cooking stove, kitchen units and bathroom fixtures. Use them as shown in the Building guide. Survival carpentry needs a carried Furniture hammer. Furniture and carpentry

Each table and desk has a fixed size. For a longer one, place matching pieces with the same woods side by side at the same height: dining tables join on any edge, desks only end to end.

Good to know. A table lamp needs a solid block counter or ledge; it cannot stand on a furniture table. Sinks, basins and bathtubs hold no water of their own, and there is no plumbing.

Wooden chests and doors are also available; see Wooden chests and Wooden doors.

Player skins

Planned, not in the game. Your explorer wears one built-in outfit with fixed colours. There is no skin editor, and no skin import or export. Player skins and skin editor

When a feature ships

A feature moves off this page only after the game ships it and its source is checked. Its own guide then replaces the entry here.

How this guide was checked

Each item comes from the feature ledger, which cites the game source for the audited version. The absence checks searched the source for block, recipe and gameplay names. This is a targeted correction, not a new check of the other missing-feature sections. Multiplayer follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357: source-checked hosted save/refusal, F6 retry, Shift+F6 recovery choice, server-owned stock/crafting and Survival recovery.
